item.title: The Synthetic Human: Where Does Human Labor End?
item.lead: The title of this section revolves around a philosophical-technical question: when a system reproduces human style, memory, and timing, what remains of the idea that the user encounters a unique person?

blocks.text: The dossier uses "synthetic human" as a boundary image. The term does not refer to a humanoid robot, but to a service that simulates the characteristics of personal attention: personalized language, recognition of previous conversations, emotional alignment, and strategic timing.

From that perspective, the value of an interaction is no longer fully linked to the identity of the writer. The value lies in the quality of the simulation. This enables a fundamental distinction: authentic personalization strengthens a genuine relationship, while synthetic personalization can become a product that sells the impression of authenticity.

The dossier observes a shift in the labor market here. Human operators can be trained to correct the output of systems, while systems increasingly take over standard work. The question then becomes not whether AI replaces employees, but which components of human empathy are economically abstracted and repackaged.

This development also has implications for responsibility. When a script, model, CRM, and operator jointly produce a conversation, it is not self-evident who is responsible for a misleading outcome. The source uses this chain as an argument for transparency and chain liability.
